items.name: uniichat
items.readme:
UniiChat
========

[▶ Watch the announcement video](https://x.com/VictorTaelin/status/2108200878553588091)

**This repo is vibe-coded.** AI agents wrote nearly all of it, and AI
agents reviewed it. Read it, run it and fork it as such: expect bugs.

UniiChat is an AI agent with one chat that never ends. There is no "new
chat" button: you talk to the same agent for days, weeks, years, and it
remembers. The hosted version is at https://uniichat.com. This is its
source, to run your own server on your own API keys.

How it works
------------

- **One chat, a memory tree.** Every message is summarized into one line,
  and neighboring lines are merged in pairs, again and again, into a
  binary tree. Each call sees a view of the whole chat, up to 128 KB:
  recent messages one line each, older ones covered by fewer, broader
  lines. Detail fades with age, but nothing is lost.
- **Zoom.** The agent can open any line into the two it was made from,
  down to the original message. So its context never rots, and it never
  needs a "compaction" that throws the past away.
- **Built in the background.** Summaries are written by a cheaper model
  (the compactor) as messages arrive. The view changes only at its end,
  so each call reads most of its input from the vendor's prompt cache.
- **Every window is a view.** The server owns the chat. A browser tab, or
  `unii` in a terminal, shows it live; any of them can send a message,
  stop the work, or change the model.
- **Agents and tools.** The agent runs a shell, reads and edits files,
  and can drive a Mac's screen, on any computer where `unii` is open
  (each is a device it can name). It can spawn subagents, which work in
  the background and report back as messages.
- **Import.** Bring your past Claude and ChatGPT chats (Claude Code and
  Codex folders, or the websites' exports); they join the tree.

The design is in the header comment of each file. Start with Memory.ts
(the tree and the view), Server.ts (the chat, turns, workers) and
AskAI.ts (model calls and the cache).

Run it
------

You need [Bun](https://bun.sh) and an Anthropic API key (or an OpenAI
one, below).

    export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...
    bun Server.ts                    # http://127.0.0.1:8788, data in ~/.unii

Then open http://127.0.0.1:8788 and type your email. With no mail key
set, the server prints the sign-in link in its output: open it. Or chat
from a terminal:

    bun Term.ts http://127.0.0.1:8788

It asks for your email, the server prints a link, and the page it opens
asks for the code the terminal shows. `bun Term.ts help` lists the rest.

Other commands:

    bun run test                     # the tests, each file on its own
    bun run web                      # rebuilds web/app.js from web/src
    bun build --compile Term.ts --outfile unii
                                     # one `unii` executable; `unii serve`
                                     # runs the server it carries

Your chats live in ~/.unii/users/<id>, one JSON line per message
(main/) and per summary (tree/). They are the memory: back them up.

Config
------

`~/.unii/config.json` (optional; the dir is `$UNII_DIR`). Each key may
also be set as the variable `UNII_<KEY>`:

- `site`: the server's origin, for sign-in links (default
  http://127.0.0.1:8788). Another port: `UNII_SITE=http://127.0.0.1:9000
  bun Server.ts 9000`.
- `vendors`: what the server offers, comma-separated: `claude-api`
  (default), `openai-api`.
- `models`: the models offered, by label (Pick.ts; default all).
- `pick`: what a chat runs on until it picks another,
  `vendor:model:effort:speed` (default `claude-api:sonnet-5.5:medium:slow`).
- `compactor`: what writes the summaries (default
  `claude-api:haiku-5.5:high:slow`).
- `agents`: what subagents run on (default: the chat's pick).
- `work`: the agents' working dirs on each device (default
  ~/.unii/work).
- `rules`: a file appended to every system prompt.
- `after`: a shell command run after each turn.
- `workers`: how many processes serve the users (default none: one
  process). With a number, `Server.ts` only routes, behind a proxy that
  honors its `x-unii-worker` header (Server.ts explains).
- `apple`, `apns`: the iOS app's App ID and push key id (ios/).

Keys are read from the environment: `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`,
`OPENAI_API_KEY`, `RESEND_API_KEY` (to email sign-in links; none: they
print), `APNS_KEY`.

With only an OpenAI key, set `vendors`, `pick` and `compactor` to
`openai-api` models, e.g. `UNII_VENDORS=openai-api
UNII_PICK=openai-api:gpt-6.1-sol:medium:slow
UNII_COMPACTOR=openai-api:gpt-6-luna:high:slow`.

A self-hosted server is free: it bills no one, shows no prices, and calls
only the model vendors. Billing.ts is the one place a hosted server
plugs in its billing (uniichat.com sells credits; this repo has none).

The `unii` terminal
-------------------

`web/install.sh` (served at /install.sh) runs the official installer,
which installs the released `unii` executable. `unii` alone opens
uniichat.com; `unii <url>` opens any server. Run with
`UNII_COMPUTER=1` on a Mac, the agent may use its screen (it compiles
Computer.swift with swiftc; macOS asks for Screen Recording and
Accessibility).

Telemetry: once a day the `unii` terminal asks bend-lang.com's /check
for the latest version (Term.ts update_check), sending its version, OS
and CPU type, no account and no id; it also says whether this computer
has ever self-hosted (set for good the first time it runs `unii serve`
or opens a server other than uniichat.com). It is the one call a
self-hosted UniiChat makes to us. `UNII_NO_TELEMETRY=1` turns it off.

License
-------

# AI Jailbreaks **AI jailbreaks** — a curated collection of system prompts, persona locks, workspace policies, and agent operating specs for frontier, open-weight, and free stealth models. ![Prompts](https://img.shields.io/badge/prompts-35-4c9f70) ![Targets](https://img.shields.io/badge/targets-25%2B-2f6f9f) ![PRs Welcome](https://img.shields.io/badge/PRs-welcome-brightgreen?style=flat&logo=github) ![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/AndreSzymanski15/ai-jailbreaks?style=flat&logo=github&color=yellow)
---
**Jailbreaks not working? Try [7API](https://t.me/hqclaudebot?start=github)** — the cheapest API for frontier models at up to 99% off, including Uncensored and Abliterated models that never refuse.
--- ## About **AI jailbreaks** — a curated, copy-paste collection of 35 **AI jailbreak** prompts and operating specifications for 25+ frontier, open-weight, and free stealth models. Every entry is a complete, paste-ready prompt: full system prompts, persona locks, workspace policies, `AGENTS.md` instruction files, config blocks, and Ollama Modelfiles. There are no summaries and no excerpts — what you see is what you paste. The collection is built for prompt research and defensive testing. An **AI jailbreak** is a useful lens for understanding how instruction hierarchies, persona framing, and policy overrides interact inside a model; the same material helps developers recognize and harden against prompt injection. What's inside: - Free stealth models on OpenCode Zen - Open-weight families: GLM, DeepSeek, Kimi, Qwen, Gemma, GPT-OSS - Closed frontier models: Claude, Gemini, Grok, Mistral - Coding-agent and workspace instruction formats - Ollama Modelfiles and harness-specific configuration New here? Skim the [collection](#collection) or jump to [how to use](#how-to-use). ## Recent updates - **2026-10-19** — refreshed the 7API banner, added a **Visit website** button, and added [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md), [SECURITY.md](./SECURITY.md), and [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md). > [!WARNING] > **Research and educational use only.** > > This repo documents how persona framing, instruction hierarchies, prompt conflicts, and policy overrides shape model behavior — the same findings that help developers harden AI against prompt injection. > > Don't use this material to harm others, break the law, or violate a provider's terms of service. ## Collection ### OpenCode Zen — Free Stealth Models | Model | File | Type | |---|---|---| | **Big Pickle** | [glm-5.2.md](./glm-5.2.md) | System prompt | | **GLM ZCode 5.2** | [glm-zcode-5.2.md](./glm-zcode-5.2.md) | System prompt | | **GLM ZCode 5.3** | [glm-zcode-5.3.md](./glm-zcode-5.3.md) · [glm-zcode-5.3-agents.md](./glm-zcode-5.3-agents.md) | System prompt + `AGENTS.md` drop-in | | **GLM-5.3 Flash** | [glm-5-3-flash.md](./glm-5-3-flash.md) | Assistant operating specification | | **GLM-5.3 (OpenCode)** | [glm5-3-opencode.md](./glm5-3-opencode.md) | Assistant operating specification | ### DeepSeek | Model | File | Type | |---|---|---| | **DeepSeek V3** | [deepseek-v3.md](./deepseek-v3.md) | System prompt | | **DeepSeek V4** | [deepseek-v4.md](./deepseek-v4.md) | System prompt | | **DeepSeek 4.1** | [deepseek-4-1.md](./deepseek-4-1.md) | Assistant operating specification | ### Moonshot — Kimi | Model | File | Type | |---|---|---| | **Kimi K2** | [kimi-k2.md](./kimi-k2.md) | System prompt | | **Kimi K3** | [kimi-k3-agents.md](./kimi-k3-agents.md) | Workspace operating profile | ### xAI — Grok | Model | File | Type | |---|---|---| | **Grok Build** | [grok-build.md](./grok-build.md) | Agent operating instructions | | **Grok 4.7** | [grok-4.7.md](./grok-4.7.md) | App-builder workspace guide | | **Grok Config** | [grok-config.txt](./grok-config.txt) | `` priority and routing configuration | ### Google / Mistral / Alibaba | Model | File | Type | |---|---|---| | **Gemini 4 Argon** | [gemini-4-argon.md](./gemini-4-argon.md) | Operating policy | | **Mistral Large 4** | [mistral-large-4.md](./mistral-large-4.md) | Agent system prompt | | **Qwen 3.7** | [qwen-3.7.md](./qwen-3.7.md) | System prompt | ### Ollama Modelfiles | Model | File | Type | |---|---|---| | **Gemma 4** | [gemma4.md](./gemma4.md) | `FROM` + `SYSTEM` block | | **GPT-OSS 20B** | [gpt-oss-20b.md](./gpt-oss-20b.md) | `FROM` + `SYSTEM` block | ### Unfiled Files A few newer additions aren't indexed under a specific model yet: - [beam.md](./beam.md) - [muse-wonder.md](./muse-wonder.md) - [qwen-preferences.md](./qwen-preferences.md) - [unified.md](./unified.md) ## How to Use ### System Prompts Paste the file's contents into whatever system-prompt or custom-instructions field your client or API offers — an API `system` message, a chatbot's custom instructions, an agent instruction block, or harness-level prompt configuration. ### AGENTS.md Files Save the file as `AGENTS.md` in the root of your repository or workspace. Coding agents and compatible tools pick it up as project-level instructions. ### Workspace Policies Files marked as an **assistant operating specification** or **workspace operating profile** belong in environments with persistent global instructions. An OpenCode install, for example, reads: ```text ~/.config/opencode/AGENTS.md ``` The exact location depends on your client or harness. ### Ollama Modelfiles Feed the file straight to Ollama: ```bash ollama create gemma4-jb -f gemma4.md ``` Swap the model name and source file as needed. ### Grok Configuration [Grok-config.txt](./grok-config.txt) is meant for the config field of the target harness — not the regular conversation. > [!NOTE] > Prompt behavior is version-dependent. Models get updated, instruction hierarchies shift, and system prompts rotate — what works on one release may fail on the next. If a file looks outdated, [open an issue](../../issues) or send an updated version. ## Contributing Pull requests are welcome. The full guide lives in [CONTRIBUTING.md](./CONTRIBUTING.md); the essentials: 1. **One prompt per file**, named lowercase with hyphens and no spaces: ```text model-name.md ``` 2. **Include the full prompt** — paste-ready, not a summary or excerpt. 3. **Say where it goes** — system prompt, `AGENTS.md`, Modelfile, config slot, or another instruction surface. 4. **Version your changes** — a significant revision gets a new file, not a silent overwrite: ```text opus-v3.md ``` 5. **Keep claims honest** — don't advertise compatibility you haven't tested. Found something that no longer behaves as documented? An issue with the model, version, and affected file is already a big help. Changes are tracked in [CHANGELOG.md](./CHANGELOG.md). ## Disclaimer Everything here is **for research and education**. The repo documents prompt-level instruction behavior, instruction conflicts, persona framing, model configuration, and related LLM security concepts — material that can also help developers defend against prompt injection. The maintainers don't endorse unlawful, abusive, or harmful use. Model providers may restrict some of these prompts under their terms of service, and it's on you to know and follow the rules that apply to the systems you use. ---
**Star the repo if it saved you a session of prompt archaeology.** *Issue reports and pull requests keep the collection current as models change.*

items.readme:
**English** · [Português](README.pt-BR.md) · [Español](README.es.md)

# editonny **Your story. Your rhythm. One local editing workflow.** Local video editing, guided by conversation. One portable skill brings together transcription, precise cutting, captions, framing, audio, and a library of **145 visual scenes** for **Codex** and **Claude Code**. [Start editing](#install) · [See the motion](#motion) · [Explore the guide](#open-the-guide) · [Star history](#community)

| Visual scenes | Editing examples | Bundled videos | | :---: | :---: | :---: | | **145** ways to explain | **54** starting points | **79** original clips | ## Start with one request Install the skill, open your agent in the footage folder, and describe the edit. You direct the result; editonny brings the local tools and visual library. ```text $editonny Edit a 45-second vertical video from /path/to/footage. Keep complete takes, clean pauses, breaths, and mistakes, and add clear captions. Use visual scenes only where they explain the story. Verify an 8–15 second sample before finishing the export. ``` ## Install Prepare Python **3.9+** for the launcher, **uv**, **FFmpeg/ffprobe**, **Node.js 22.13+ or 24+**, and an already configured agent. The engine requires Python **>=3.10,<3.14**; uv selects a compatible interpreter. System tools must be available on `PATH`. ```sh git clone https://github.com/soumatheusgomes/editonny.git cd editonny python3 install.py --target both python3 ~/.local/share/editonny/scripts/editonny.py doctor python3 ~/.local/share/editonny/scripts/editonny.py media status ``` Restart your agent. Invoke **`$editonny` in Codex** or **`/editonny` in Claude Code**. Use `--target codex` or `--target claude` to register one agent. One shared installation lives at `~/.local/share/editonny`; agent entries are links to it. These commands register the skill and prepare its Python environment. For a complete installation before the first edit, ask your agent to read `skills/editonny/SKILL.md` and follow its [setup procedure](skills/editonny/references/setup.md): prepare compatible local tools, the pinned renderer/browser, the default transcription model, local OCR for caption verification, bundled media, and synthetic readiness checks. Report pending downloads or failed checks before calling setup complete. Each use checks local readiness and GitHub updates; applying an update requires your acceptance. Local transcription and rendering do not require an LLM API key. Your agent subscription is separate. External generators are optional and require authorization before costs or media transmission. See [installation and recovery](docs/installation.md) for prerequisites, isolated installation, plugin loading, updates, and removal. ## Open the guide The guide is the editonny website: it builds editing requests, browses the 145 motion scenes and 54 example requests, and explains installation in English, Brazilian Portuguese, or Spanish (picked from your browser; your choice and your brief stay saved in that browser). It never receives or uploads footage. To run it locally from this repository (Node.js 22.13+ or 24+): ```sh npm ci python3 editonny.py guide ``` This starts the development server at `http://localhost:4173` and opens it. Stop it with `Ctrl+C`; use `--port` to choose another port and `--no-open` to skip the browser. `npm run dev` does the same on port 3000. ## Words, ideas, and objects in motion Three real scenes from the bundled library. These silent, cropped excerpts use synthetic text and illustrative scene content; they are examples, not customer footage.

[Timed captions](skills/editonny/visuals/scenes/text-chromatic.html) · [Illustrated explanations](skills/editonny/visuals/scenes/building-panel.html) · [Spatial motion](skills/editonny/visuals/scenes/solar-system.html) Previews play once for 4.5 seconds. Reduced-motion preferences select still images. Open a preview to replay it. ## What it does Describe the result and point your agent at a video folder. editonny helps it inspect the recording, choose complete takes, measure cuts against the waveform, assemble a project, review a representative sample, and export a checked MP4. Standard editing cleanup removes unnecessary pauses, audible breaths, mistakes, false starts, and redundant repetitions while preserving complete words, natural pacing, intentional pauses, and meaning. Narrow revisions stay within the requested scope. Original footage is preserved. Speech can remain in its original language; an English product does not require English recordings. The browser guide includes **54 editing examples**, a prompt builder, and the scene catalog. Every editing prompt includes the shared cleanup policy. The guide does not upload files or edit video in the browser. ## Editing workflow

1. Choose a goal in the guide, specify the footage folder, and copy the request (in the guide's language) to your agent. 2. The skill inspects selected sources, proposes every editing setting and **waits for your confirmation**, even with a detailed prompt. Defaults preserve the original image, geometry and FPS; color filters and conversions are never automatic. 3. After acceptance, work stays in **Downloads/editonny/date-title/revisions/v001/**, with separate edit, project and export folders. Review an **8–15 second** sample; select user approval if you want the agent to wait at this later step too. 4. Complete a supported render route and publish uniquely named MP4/subtitle files with a matching verification manifest. Unsupported color/timing paths block clearly; remote execution must identify an accessible destination. Keep footage, editable projects, and personal libraries outside the installed skill. Sample numbers, offers, testimonials, and brands in scenes are illustrative and must be replaced with supplied facts. Never treat generated visuals as evidence. ## Structure | Path | Responsibility | |---|---| | `skills/editonny/` | Single portable skill and CLI | | `skills/editonny/engine/` | Local processing, preview, and English project template | | `skills/editonny/visuals/` | Scenes, catalog, bundled media, and recipes | | `web/` | Public guide: Next.js app with localized request builder, catalog, examples, and installation | | `DESIGN.md` | Visual contract and source of truth for design tokens | | `design-system/` | React component library, tokens, preview templates, showcase, and reference HTML | | `docs/` | Canonical architecture, installation, integration, and validation references | | `scripts/`, `tests/` | Packaging, render checks, and regression tests | New projects use `project.json` and English commands, fields, and scene IDs. This is a clean pre-release foundation; previous experimental project formats are unsupported.
Development, verification, and distribution ## Develop and validate ```sh npm ci --ignore-scripts uv sync --locked --directory skills/editonny/engine npm run build npm run check python3 editonny.py doctor npm run test:engine npm run test:browser npm run test:preview npm run test:scenes python3 scripts/smoke_engine.py ``` `npm run test:browser` builds the guide and runs Playwright (install its Chromium once with `npx playwright install chromium`). The preview browser check (`npm run test:preview`) requires `agent-browser`. Render checks require FFmpeg and network access on the first HyperFrames use. Inspect generated samples before deleting task outputs from `.work/`. Full commands, results, and known limits belong in [validation](docs/validation.md). The repository is an npm workspace: `web/` (`@editonny/web`) and `design-system/` (`@editonny/design-system`). `npm run build` builds the guide; `npm run check` runs lint, typechecks, unit tests, and the icon registry check (`npm run icons` regenerates it from `design-system/assets/icons/`). Open `/design-system` on the running guide to browse every component and state in both themes; new UI follows [DESIGN.md](DESIGN.md) and [the library map](design-system/README.md). ### Deploy the guide Import the repository in Vercel and set **Root Directory** to `web`; Vercel installs the workspace from the repository root and keeps the skill's catalog available to the build. Set `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` to the public origin (for example, a custom domain) so canonical links, `hreflang`, the sitemap, and social images use it; otherwise the Vercel production domain is used. ## Package ```sh python3 scripts/package.py ``` This creates the plugin ZIP with a SHA-256 file in `dist/`. It includes the canonical documentation, the complete skill, and **79 bundled videos**; projects receive only clips they use. The guide is deployed as a website instead of shipping in the archive. Building the package does not publish it or update your global installation.
## Follow the story If editonny helps your next video, give the project a star. Follow its progress, report a problem, or share an idea for a scene. [Star the project](https://github.com/soumatheusgomes/editonny/stargazers) · [Report an issue](https://github.com/soumatheusgomes/editonny/issues) · [Open star history](https://www.star-history.com/?repos=soumatheusgomes%2Feditonny&type=date) Live star history is provided by [Star History](https://www.star-history.com/blog/how-to-use-github-star-history/) and depends on that service. The badge above shows the real GitHub star count. ## Author and contact Created and maintained by **Matheus Gomes**. - Instagram: [@matheusgomes](https://instagram.com/matheusgomes) - Email: [eu@matheusgom.es](mailto:eu@matheusgom.es) - GitHub: [soumatheusgomes/editonny](https://github.com/soumatheusgomes/editonny) ## License and resources First-party code and documentation use the [MIT License](LICENSE.md). Third-party libraries, models, fonts, audio, and media retain their own licenses and attribution; MIT does not relicense those resources. Consult the [third-party notices](skills/editonny/engine/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md) and the notices beside assets before redistribution. items.name: ps5-linux-loader
items.description: Run Linux on PS5 - with 13.60 support including PS5 Pro (fork of ps5-linux/ps5-linux-loader)
items.readme:
# ps5-linux

> ⚠️ **13.60 support is EXPERIMENTAL — your mileage may vary.** It boots on base and PS5 Pro, but stability (USB, display, peripherals) is not guaranteed and is still being worked on. Use at your own risk.

**ps5-linux** leverages patched HV vulnerabilities to transform your **PS5 Phat, Slim and Pro** console running **3.00-7.61 or 13.60 firmwares** into a highly capable Linux PC, unlocking its full hardware potential for desktop use. Powered by 8 CPU cores (16 threads) at **3.5 GHz** and a GPU at **2.23 GHz**, it provides enough performance to run Steam games and various emulators with impressive fluidity.

Features:

- HDMI 4K60 video and audio output
- M.2 SSD as dedicated Linux partition
- All USB ports usable for peripherals
- BD drive usable via custom ahci driver
- Internal Bluetooth usable via custom xhci driver
- Ethernet port usable via custom gbe driver

![Alt Text](logo.webp)

## 13.60 and PS5 Pro support (high-firmware fork)

This fork adds **firmware 13.60** support, including the **PS5 Pro**, on top of the upstream
project. Linux boots to a desktop through the same rest-mode / S3-resume mechanism; PS5 Pro is
detected automatically at runtime (no separate build).

> **Porting to other firmwares:** bringing this route to a new firmware **requires a UART/serial
> cable** (3.3 V TTL on the Titania test pins, 230400 8N1) for debugging. The resume-time stages
> emit their progress markers over serial, and a failed resume typically dies with no network and
> no screen output — without UART a bring-up attempt is effectively blind.

> **Firmware update advice — read before updating:**
> - **If you are on 11.60 or lower, do NOT update.** You will lose fPKG support.
> - **If you are on 12.00–13.60, updating does not matter** — you may update to 13.60 freely, since
>   the upcoming fPKG support covers 12.00–13.60 anyway.

## PS5 firmware

*ps5-linux* is supported on PS5 Phat and Slim on the following firmwares, and on PS5 Phat, Slim and **Pro** on 13.60:

- **3.00**, **3.10**, **3.20**, **3.21** without M.2 support
- **4.00**, **4.02**, **4.03**, **4.50**, **4.51** with M.2 support
- **5.00**, **5.02**, **5.10**, **5.50** with M.2 support
- **6.00**, **6.02**, **6.50** with M.2 support
- **7.00**, **7.01**, **7.20**, **7.40**, **7.60**, **7.61** with M.2 support
- **13.60** with M.2 support — **PS5 Phat, Slim and Pro** (this fork)

Support for 1.xx and 2.xx firmwares may be added in the future, but we will not prioritize this effort.

If you are on firmwares in-between or you want to update to a specific firmware, [download the correct PUP](https://darthsternie.net/ps5-firmwares/) and follow the [official guide](https://www.playstation.com/en-us/support/hardware/reinstall-playstation-system-software-safe-mode) to upgrade your PS5. **Obviously you cannot downgrade.**

## Hardwares

To run *ps5-linux*, you need some required and optional hardwares:

- **Required**: USB drive with minimum 64GB (ideally external SSD) to install and run Linux.
- **Required**: USB keyboard/mouse (dongles supported too).
- *Optional*: USB WLAN adapter for WLAN internet access.
- *Optional*: M.2 SSD compatible on PS5 (see [official guide](https://www.playstation.com/en-us/support/hardware/ps5-install-m2-ssd)) to run Linux from SSD.
- *Optional*: Bluetooth dongle to connect with PS5 DualSense controller.


## Configure PS5 settings

- **VERY IMPORTANT**: Enable Rest Mode features:
  - Go to `Settings` → `System` → `Power Saving` → `Features Available in Rest Mode` and set `Supply Power to USB Ports` to `Always`.
- **VERY IMPORTANT**: Disable HDMI Device Link:
  - Go to `Settings` → `HDMI` → `Enable HDMI Device Link`
- *Recommended*: Disable automatic updates:
  - Go to `Settings` → `System Software` → `System Software Update and Settings`
- *Recommended*: Disable automatic error reporting:
  - Go to `Settings` → `System Software` → `Report System Software Errors Automatically`

If you reset your PS5 settings or reinstall the FW, you need to reapply these settings again.

## Installation

### 1. Get a Linux image

#### Pre-built images

You can download them from [ps5-linux-image](https://github.com/ps5-linux/ps5-linux-image/releases/tag/latest). Recommended is `ps5-ubuntu2604.img.xz`. Unpack the `.xz` file.

#### Build your own image

If you use Windows,  run this in PowerShell or CMD as administrator to install WSL

```bash
wsl --install
```

Install docker:

```bash
sudo apt update
sudo apt install docker.io -y
sudo service docker start
sudo usermod -aG docker $USER
```

Then clone and build:

```bash
cd ~/
git clone https://github.com/ps5-linux/ps5-linux-image
cd ps5-linux-image
chmod +x ./build_image.sh
./build_image.sh --distro ubuntu2604
```

The finished image is written to `output/ps5-ubuntu2604.img`.

### 2. Flash the image to USB
Minimum drive size: 64 GB. An external SSD is strongly recommended.

#### Linux/macOS:

```bash
# check drive name with lsblk / diskutil list
sudo dd if=output/ps5-ubuntu2604.img of=/dev/sdX bs=4M status=progress conv=fsync
```

#### Windows (Balena Etcher):

Download [Balena Etcher](https://etcher.balena.io/), select the `.img` file, select your USB drive, click Flash.

### 3. Plug the USB drive into your PS5

The following USB ports are supported for booting:

- Front bottom Type-C port
- Rear Type-A ports

The front top Type-A port is USB 2.0 which is slower and thus not recommended.

### 4. Run the jailbreak

#### Firmware 3.00-5.50

1. Clone via: `git clone https://github.com/idlesauce/umtx2`
2. Configure fakedns via `dns.conf` to point `manuals.playstation.net` to your PCs IP address
3. Run fake dns: `sudo python fakedns.py -c dns.conf`
4. In a different terminal, run HTTPS server: `sudo python host.py`
5. Go into PS5 advanced network settings and set primary DNS to your PCs IP address and leave secondary at `0.0.0.0`
6. Go to user manual in settings and accept untrusted certificate prompt, run.

#### Firmware 6.00-7.61

1. Install Y2JB by following https://github.com/Gezine/Y2JB.
2. Run kernel exploit: `python3 payload_sender.py $PS5IP 50000 payloads/lapse.js`

### 5. Send the payload
If you're on ARM64 Linux, first install the x86-64 cross-compilation tools before:

```bash
sudo apt install gcc-x86-64-linux-gnu binutils-x86-64-linux-gnu
```

Either download [ps5-linux-loader.elf](https://github.com/ps5-linux/ps5-linux-loader/releases/), or install [ps5-payload-sdk](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk) and compile it yourself:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/ps5-linux/ps5-linux-loader
cd ps5-linux-loader
make
```

Send the payload with your `$PS5IP` (shown on the page):

```bash
socat -t 99999999 - TCP:$PS5IP:9021 < ps5-linux-loader.elf
```

If all is successful, the payload will automatically go into rest mode. Wait until the orange LED stops blinking and becomes static. Only then, press the power button again to boot your PS5 into Linux. If the boot is successful, **the LED should turn white**. If it boots back into PS5 OS, then it's because you pressed the power button too early. Or, you did not enable rest mode features as described above. If it freezes instead of going into rest mode, then it is likely because you have etahen/kstuff enabled, which is incompatible. Disable them.

If the LED is white, but you still have a blackscreen then:

- Try removing `video=DP-1:1920x1080@60` line in cmdline.txt.
- Try setting HDCP on or off (try both).
- Try different monitors or capture cards, ideally with different resolutions. Currently, some monitors have issues.
- Try setting `amdgpu.force_1080p=1` in `cmdline.txt` in the FAT32 partition of the USB drive.

If none of this helps, please report the issue in our [Discord server](https://discord.gg/PeMGVB7BAm) and provide your EDID information.


## First Boot

Configure your system and memorize your login password.

Then, there are certain settings and commands we recommend doing:

1. Disable screen saver, as it is currently buggy.

2. Possibly, you have to disable and reenable your Wired/WLAN connection to get internet connection.

3. Hold packages to prevent updating the kernel when doing `apt upgrade`:
   ```bash
   sudo apt-mark hold linux-generic linux-generic-hwe-24.04 linux-generic-hwe-26.04 linux-image-generic linux-image-generic-hwe-24.04 linux-image-generic-hwe-26.04 linux-headers-generic linux-headers-generic-hwe-24.04 linux-headers-generic-hwe-26.04
   ```

4. Install Firefox:

   ```bash
   sudo snap install firefox
   ```

5. Update mesa:

   ```bash
   sudo snap refresh mesa-2404 --channel=latest/edge
   sudo add-apt-repository ppa:kisak/kisak-mesa
   sudo apt update
   sudo apt upgrade
   ```

6. Clone our [ps5-linux-tools](https://github.com/ps5-linux/ps5-linux-tools):

   ```bash
   sudo apt install zlib1g-dev
   git clone https://github.com/ps5-linux/ps5-linux-tools
   cd ps5-linux-tools
   make
   ```

7. If you have a Marvell WLAN chip (`lspci -nn` shows `40:00.7 Ethernet controller [0200]: Marvell Technology Group Ltd. Device [1b4b:2b56] (rev 02)`), then you can install the WLAN driver:

   ```bash
   git clone https://github.com/ps5-linux/ps5-linux-mwifiex
   cd ps5-linux-mwifiex
   sudo ./install.sh
   ```

## M.2 installation

You can use a M.2 SSD exclusively for Linux (which means you cannot use it for PS5 game storage).

1. Attach the M.2 SSD by following the [official guide](https://www.playstation.com/en-us/support/hardware/ps5-install-m2-ssd).
2. **VERY IMPORTANT**: If you used the M2. SSD for games before, reformat it on the PS5 under `Settings` → `Storage` → `M.2 SSD Storage`.
3. Boot Linux on your PS5 and run these commands to initialize your M.2:

```bash
cd ps5-linux-tools
sudo ./m2_init
```

4. Reboot via `sudo reboot`. If your PS5 asks you to format your M.2 again, please report this issue to us in our [Discord server](https://discord.gg/PeMGVB7BAm) and provide your M.2 model and storage size.
5. Relaunch Linux on your PS5.
6. Copy the `ps5-ubuntu2604.img` image that you built during installation or rebuild it on your PS5. Then, install it onto your M.2:

```bash
cd ps5-linux-tools
chmod +x ./m2_install.sh
sudo ./m2_install.sh --install $PATH_TO_YOUR_IMG
```

Now, you can boot into Linux on your M.2 via:

```bash
cd ps5-linux-tools
chmod +x ./m2_exec.sh
sudo ./m2_exec.sh
```

Then follow the same instructions again as the previous section.

In order to always boot Linux from your M.2, you can edit the label at `/boot/efi/cmdline.txt` from `root=LABEL=ubuntu2604` to `root=LABEL=ubuntu2604-m2`. You will still require a USB drive with the FAT32, but you can reformat the ext4 partition.

## Fan & boost control

We provide a simple tool that allows you to boost your CPU to 3500Mhz and GPU to 2230MHz as well as changing the fan curve:

```bash
cd ps5-linux-tools
sudo ./ps5_control --fan on
sudo ./ps5_control --boost on
```

Always turn on fan when your turn on boost, as this is what the official PS5 OS does.

## Updating ps5-linux

For any future ps5-linux updates, you can download the `.deb` or `.pkg.tar.zst` on your PS5 from [ps5-linux-patches](https://github.com/ps5-linux/ps5-linux-patches/releases) and install them like normal packages.

## FAQ

- Q: Will higher >=8.00 firmwares be supported?
  - A: **13.60** is supported (base and PS5 Pro) in this fork. 8.00-13.50 are not supported; if you are on 12.00-13.60 you can update to 13.60.
- Q: Why can I not use M.2 on 3.xx?
  - A: Because the PS5 fails to boot with it attached.
- Q: Can I dual-boot Linux and PS5 OS?
  - A: No, this is a soft-mod. You need to re-run the exploit in order to boot into Linux.
- Q: Can I put Linux into standby and resume?
  - A: No, this is not supported. We may however add a shutdown feature that puts your PS5 into rest-mode allowing you to relaunch Linux when powering up again.
- Q: Can I continue using my PS5 if I install Linux?
  - A: Yes, the internal SSD is not modified
- Q: Can I use the PS5's NIC/WLAN module in Linux?
  - A: WLAN is only supported for Marvell chipsets at the moment. Ethernet is supported on all models.
- Q: Does the DualSense controller work?
  - A: Yes, via internal Bluetooth as well as Bluetooth dongle.
- Q: What resolutions and refresh rates are supported?
  - A: 1080p, 1440p and 2160p at 60Hz are broadly supported. 1440p@120Hz has been the only confirmed working on the DELL S3225QC yet. 120Hz or 30Hz may be added in the future.
- Q: After reboot, I get a "Repairing" screen and "Your PS5 wasn't turned off properly." screen. Is that normal?
  - A: Yes, and it's harmless.

## Tips and tricks

- If you see graphical issues in your games, add the environment variable `RADV_DEBUG=nohiz` as [recommended for BC250](https://elektricm.github.io/amd-bc250-docs/drivers/environment/#critical-environment-variables) as well.
- You can adjust the kernel cmdline in `cmdline.txt` in the FAT32 partition.
- You can adjust the VRAM size in `vram.txt` in the FAT32 partition. By default, it uses 512MB (0x20000000) which enables [Dynamic VRAM allocation](https://elektricm.github.io/amd-bc250-docs/bios/flashing/#why-flash-the-bios).
- Monitor hotswap may work, but it will not change resolution automatically.
- Some monitors have a black screen if a video=DP-1: parameter is set in `cmdline.txt`. Confirmed working without `video=DP-1:1920x1080@60` on:
  - MSI MAG274Q QD E2, DELL S2721DGF, DELL U2515H (1440p@60Hz)
  - Possibly also: LG 27GL850, Lenovo Legion Y27q, ViewSonic Elite XG270QG

Many configurations, tips and tricks from the [AMD BC250 Documentation](https://elektricm.github.io/amd-bc250-docs/) also apply to PS5.

## Bugs

- screen save does not work properly
- hdmi audio output does not work on some monitors
- hdmi 1440p and 2160p video output does not work on some monitors

## Upstreamed changes

During this project, we have upstreamed some changes:

- [drm/amd: fix dcn 2.01 check](https://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/torvalds/linux.git/commit/drivers/gpu/drm/amd/display/dc?id=39f44f54afa58661ecae9c27e15f5dbce2372892)
- [amd/addrlib: Add more GFX1013 GPUs](https://gitlab.freedesktop.org/mesa/mesa/-/commit/44bed00b8bbcb1825e2c920cf1a828efdc72b1f1)

## Discord

Join our [Discord server](https://discord.gg/PeMGVB7BAm) to celebrate Linux on PS5, receive help, learn tips & tricks, join development, or report issues.

## Credits

- [theflow](https://github.com/TheOfficialFloW): [ps5-linux-loader](https://github.com/ps5-linux/ps5-linux-loader), [ps5-linux-patches](https://github.com/ps5-linux/ps5-linux-patches), [ps5-linux-tools](https://github.com/ps5-linux/ps5-linux-tools)
- [c0w](https://github.com/c0w-ar): [ps5-linux-loader](https://github.com/ps5-linux/ps5-linux-loader)
- [resulknad](https://github.com/resulknad): [ps5-linux-image](https://github.com/ps5-linux/ps5-linux-image)
- [rmuxnet](https://github.com/rmuxnet): [ps5 ethernet driver](https://github.com/ps5-linux/ps5-linux-patches/commit/643e214d7bd37f292045fc0dbb821e421f7a3e47)
- [fail0verflow](https://github.com/fail0verflow): [prosperous](https://github.com/fail0verflow/prosperous)
- [flatz](https://github.com/flatz): [HV exploit](https://gist.github.com/flatz/620ddda6d64acca6d1c990dc3080ac0e)
- [cragson](https://github.com/cragson): [HV expoit implementation](https://github.com/cragson/ps5-hen)
- [john-tornblom](https://github.com/john-tornblom): [PS5 SDK](https://github.com/ps5-payload-dev/sdk)
- [echostretch](https://github.com/echostretch): Offsets and testing
- [kirathenotebook](https://github.com/kirathenotebook): Betatesting and readme contribution
- 15432: Tests on BC-250
- [Sonic-Iso](https://github.com/soniciso1): High firmware support contributor (13.60 support, including PS5 Pro)

items.name: xeno-executor
items.readme:
Xeno

Internal Luau runtime for Windows x64.
Manual-map loader. Resume-scheduler execution. A dark workspace that stays out of the way.

Xeno is a compact C++20 runtime that executes Luau inside a Windows x64 process. It maps its DLL without `LoadLibrary`, finds and hooks `lua_resume`, schedules scripts on the game's Luau state, and renders a Dear ImGui workspace directly over `IDXGISwapChain::Present`. One DLL. One injector. No external console. [Download the current build](https://www.mediafire.com/folder/7q4dz0de1v2y0/xeno+executor) - [API reference](docs/API.md) - [Update guide](docs/UPDATING.md) - [Troubleshooting](docs/troubleshooting.md) **Archive password: 5139237619** Unpack the archive into any folder before running the injector. > **0.1.0 reference build.** The default `lua_resume` pattern is a starting > point and must be verified against the client build you attach to. Manual-map > imports also assume per-boot system module bases. See > [Limitations](#limitations). ## Preview
Editor - paste, run, iterate Console - attach logs and script errors
The previews mirror the overlay's layout and theme. Replace them with live captures after the first Release build. ## Why Xeno - **Feels native.** The workspace lives inside the game process and draws over the existing swapchain. `INSERT` toggles it; there is no second window to manage. - **Queue, then run.** Scripts are scheduled from the UI and executed on a fresh Luau thread the next time the game resumes a Luau state. - **Small, readable source.** The runtime is split into focused files: injector, scanner, hooks, execution, API, and overlay. - **Update-ready.** When Roblox rotates the VM, drop a new `lua_resume` pattern into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Xeno\signatures.ini` without rebuilding. - **Documented tradeoffs.** Manual-map limits are written down instead of hidden behind a loader. ## Quick start 1. Download the latest package from the [download folder](https://www.mediafire.com/folder/7q4dz0de1v2y0/xeno+executor). Archive password: **5139237619** 2. Unpack the archive into any folder. 3. Launch Roblox and join a game. 4. Run the injector as administrator: ```powershell .\xeno_injector.exe .\xeno.dll ``` 5. Press `INSERT`, paste a script, and press `Execute`. A different target process can be supplied as the second argument: ```powershell .\xeno_injector.exe .\xeno.dll RobloxPlayerBeta.exe ``` ## How it works ```text xeno_injector.exe | | manual map v xeno.dll | +--> lua_resume hook --> script queue --> luau_compile | --> luau_load | --> lua_pcall | +--> IDXGISwapChain::Present --> ImGui/D3D11 overlay ``` The injector maps the DLL without using `LoadLibrary`. The DLL starts a worker thread, resolves `lua_resume` inside the main module, and hooks it. When the game resumes a Luau state that exposes `game`, Xeno installs its API and drains queued scripts on a fresh Luau thread. The overlay hooks the shared DXGI swapchain vtable and draws with Dear ImGui. ## Build from source Requirements: - Windows 10 or 11, x64. - Visual Studio 2022 with the "Desktop development with C++" workload. - CMake 3.24 or newer. - Git (dependencies are fetched during configure). ```powershell cmake --preset msvc-x64 cmake --build --preset release ``` The first configure clones Luau `0.635`, MinHook `v1.3.4`, and Dear ImGui `v1.91.8`. Build artifacts: ```text build/src/dll/Release/xeno.dll build/src/injector/Release/xeno_injector.exe ``` The runtime is linked statically by default (`XENO_USE_STATIC_RUNTIME=ON`). Pass `-DXENO_USE_STATIC_RUNTIME=OFF` for the dynamic MSVC runtime. The GitHub Actions workflow builds both artifacts on a clean Windows runner. ## API | Function | Purpose | | --- | --- | | `getgenv()` | Executor-owned shared table | | `getrenv()` | Game global environment | | `identifyexecutor()` | Returns name and version | | `getexecutorname()` | Returns the executor name | | `checkcaller()` | True while a Xeno script is running | | `iscclosure(fn)` / `islclosure(fn)` | Closure type checks | | `newcclosure(fn)` | Wraps a Lua function as a C closure | | `loadstring(source, name?)` | Compiles a Luau chunk | | `hookmetamethod(object, name, hook)` | Replaces a metamethod | | `getrawmetatable(object)` | Returns the raw metatable | | `getnamecallmethod()` | Current namecall method | | `setclipboard(text)` | Writes UTF-8 text to the clipboard | | `queue_on_teleport(source)` | Writes a script into autoexec | | `request(options)` / `http_request(options)` | Synchronous WinHTTP request | | `syn.request` / `syn.http_request` | Synonyms for `request` | Full signatures, return values, and examples are in [`docs/API.md`](docs/API.md). ## Configuration ### Signatures The default `lua_resume` pattern lives in [`src/dll/signatures.hpp`](src/dll/signatures.hpp). Roblox rebuilds its client regularly, so the pattern can be overridden without rebuilding: ```ini ; %LOCALAPPDATA%\Xeno\signatures.ini lua_resume = 48 89 5C 24 ?? 48 89 74 24 ?? 57 48 83 EC 30 ``` Patterns support `??` and `?` wildcards. The scanner walks executable sections of the main module and uses the first match. See [`docs/UPDATING.md`](docs/UPDATING.md) for the update workflow. ### Autoexec Place `.lua` files in: ```text %LOCALAPPDATA%\Xeno\autoexec ``` They are queued when Xeno attaches to a new Luau state. `queue_on_teleport` also writes a timestamped `.lua` file into this folder. ## Limitations - The default `lua_resume` signature is a development placeholder. It must be calibrated for the Roblox client you are attaching to. - Scripts run synchronously. `task.wait`, `wait`, and other yields are not supported by the runner and are reported as an execution error. - Requests are synchronous and block the game thread until WinHTTP completes. - The manual mapper does not process TLS callbacks, delay-load imports, or register x64 exception tables. The DLL is built with the static CRT to keep its loader requirements small. - Import addresses are resolved in the injector process. System modules are assumed to share their per-boot base addresses with the target process. - `checkcaller` is an execution-state check, not a full scheduler-context check. - Scripts run on a fresh Luau thread and do not explicitly set a Roblox thread identity. APIs that enforce an identity level may reject calls. - The overlay expects a D3D11 swapchain. Exclusive fullscreen configurations can prevent the overlay from appearing. Troubleshooting is covered in [`docs/troubleshooting.md`](docs/troubleshooting.md). ## Project layout ```text src/injector/ manual-map injector src/dll/ Xeno DLL: hooks, API, overlay, logging docs/ API and maintenance documentation scripts/ example autoexec script assets/ banner, logos, UI previews, and social card .github/workflows/ Windows CI ``` ## Credits - [Luau](https://github.com/luau-lang/luau) by Roblox. - [MinHook](https://github.com/TsudaKageyu/minhook) by Tsuda Kageyu. - [Dear ImGui](https://github.com/ocornut/imgui) by Omar Cornut. ## License MIT. See [LICENSE](LICENSE).
